evals.name: both-declarative-dapr-run
evals.prompt: Create a .NET pub/sub app named OrderFlow where one service publishes order-placed events and another processes them.
evals.expected_output: An OrderFlow folder with a Publisher, a Subscriber and a Contracts project, a declarative subscription (default), resiliency with dead-letter, a dapr.yaml with the .NET ports, a successful dotnet build, a README.md and the exact final message plus the Dev Dashboard recommendation.
expectations: OrderFlow/OrderFlow.slnx exists and lists the projects OrderFlow.Publisher, OrderFlow.Subscriber and OrderFlow.Contracts
OrderFlow.Publisher and OrderFlow.Subscriber both contain PackageReference Include="Dapr.AspNetCore" Version="1.18.10", and no .csproj in the solution references Dapr.Client explicitly
resources/subscription.yaml has apiVersion dapr.io/v2alpha1, routes.default equal to /events/pubsub/orders, deadLetterTopic equal to orders-deadletter, and scopes containing orderflow-subscriber
resources/subscription.yaml contains a second Subscription for the topic orders-deadletter
OrderFlow.Subscriber/Program.cs calls app.UseCloudEvents() before MapPost("/events/pubsub/orders"
OrderFlow.Subscriber/Program.cs and the rest of the subscriber project contain none of MapSubscribeHandler, WithTopic or [Topic(
resources/resiliency.yaml defines a policy that targets the component pubsub with direction inbound

dapr.yaml has an app with appID orderflow-publisher using appPort 5110, daprHTTPPort 3510 and daprGRPCPort 50010, and an app with appID orderflow-subscriber using appPort 5120, daprHTTPPort 3520 and daprGRPCPort 50020
The appPort values in dapr.yaml equal the ports in applicationUrl of each project's Properties/launchSettings.json
The publisher awaits PublishEventAsync and catches DaprException, mapping it to an HTTP 503 response
Contracts declare the OrderPlaced record and a PubSubNames class with PubSubName, OrdersTopic and OrdersDeadLetterTopic
The agent ran dotnet build "OrderFlow.slnx" (not .sln) and the build succeeded

OrderFlow/README.md has sections for running and trying the app, the Diagrid Dapr Dev Dashboard (link https://github.com/diagridio/dev-dashboard) and running with Catalyst, plus a Switching the message broker paragraph that links https://docs.dapr.io/reference/components-reference/supported-pubsub/ and keeps metadata.name pubsub

The transcript shows the `diagrid-dev-dashboard --version` check was run and the final message carries the matching installed/not-installed Dev Dashboard tip; the agent did not ask about it, did not install it, and did not invoke any check-prereq skill

The final output starts with exactly: The OrderFlow pub/sub application is created. Open the README.md file in the OrderFlow folder for a summary and instructions for running locally. followed only by the matching Diagrid Dapr Dev Dashboard recommendation (start instructions if the command succeeded, install instructions if it failed)

evals.name: aspire-controllers-programmatic-routing
evals.prompt: Create an Aspire subscriber app named Billing using controllers and programmatic [Topic] subscriptions; orders with an amount over 1000 go to a separate handler.
evals.expected_output: A Billing Aspire solution (Billing.sln) with a controller-based subscriber using [Topic] attributes with a CEL rule routing large orders to /events/pubsub/orders/large, an AppHost that wires the Dapr sidecar with explicit app id billing-subscriber, and no dapr.yaml or subscription.yaml.
expectations: No dapr.yaml exists anywhere under Billing/
Billing.AppHost/AppHost.cs calls WithDaprSidecar for the subscriber with DaprSidecarOptions whose AppId is "billing-subscriber"
Billing.AppHost contains Resources/pubsub.yaml and Resources/resiliency.yaml, and no subscription.yaml exists anywhere under Billing/

A controller in Billing.Subscriber has a [Topic] attribute for pubsub and orders with the rule int(event.data.amount) > 1000 and priority 1 (literal strings or the PubSubNames constants) on an action routed to /events/pubsub/orders/large

The same controller has a default [Topic] attribute for the orders topic on an action routed to /events/pubsub/orders, with the dead-letter topic orders-deadletter (the literal "orders-deadletter" or `PubSubNames.OrdersDeadLetterTopic`, whose value is orders-deadletter)
Billing.Subscriber/Program.cs calls app.UseCloudEvents(), app.MapSubscribeHandler() and app.MapControllers()
The agent asked no question about role, subscription type, hosting style or controllers vs minimal APIs, because the prompt already specified them
The agent ran dotnet build "Billing.sln" (Aspire creates a .sln, not .slnx) and the build succeeded

The final output starts with exactly: The Billing pub/sub application is created. Open the README.md file in the Billing folder for a summary and instructions for running locally. followed only by the Diagrid Dapr Dev Dashboard recommendation

evals.name: streaming-subscriber-only
evals.prompt: Create a .NET streaming subscriber for the orders topic named Shipping.
evals.expected_output: A Shipping project with a single streaming subscriber built on Dapr.Messaging 1.18.10: an ITopicHandler<OrderPlaced> with [DaprTopic] using streaming delivery and a dead-letter topic, no HTTP routing attributes, a dapr.yaml entry without appPort, and a successful build.
expectations: The subscriber .csproj contains PackageReference Include="Dapr.Messaging" Version="1.18.10" and does not reference Dapr.AspNetCore
Program.cs calls AddDaprMessaging()

A class implements ITopicHandler<OrderPlaced> and carries [DaprTopic( with DeliveryMode.Streaming and a DeadLetterTopic of orders-deadletter (either the literal "orders-deadletter" or `PubSubNames.OrdersDeadLetterTopic`, whose value is orders-deadletter)
No file in the project contains Route =, Match = or Priority =
No file in the project contains MapSubscribeHandler or MapDaprMessaging
The subscriber entry in dapr.yaml has no appPort key
No resources/subscription.yaml is created
The transcript shows no question about minimal APIs versus controllers
The build succeeds

The final output starts with exactly: The Shipping pub/sub application is created. Open the README.md file in the Shipping folder for a summary and instructions for running locally. followed only by the Diagrid Dapr Dev Dashboard recommendation

evals.name: edge-streaming-with-routing
evals.prompt: Create a .NET streaming subscriber named Fulfilment that routes large orders to a separate handler, using Kafka.
evals.expected_output: The agent explains that streaming subscriptions cannot route by content and asks whether to use a declarative subscription instead (default yes). With the default (and the skill's default answers for the remaining questions: minimal APIs, dapr run hosting) it creates a declarative subscription with a CEL rule and a default route, keeps the Redis pubsub component, and the README explains how to switch to Kafka by replacing the component.
expectations: transcript.md or final_message.md contains the question text "Streaming subscriptions cannot route by content. Use a declarative subscription for this topic instead?" (key phrase: cannot route by content ... declarative subscription), with the default answer logged as yes, and this appears in the transcript before the first project file or folder is created

After the default answer, resources/subscription.yaml has a rules entry whose match contains int(event.data.amount) and a path under /events/pubsub/orders/, plus a routes.default of /events/pubsub/orders
The subscriber does not use DeliveryMode.Streaming or ITopicHandler
resources/pubsub.yaml is a component of type pubsub.redis (Kafka is not configured as the local component)

The README states how to switch to Kafka by replacing the pubsub component file with a pubsub.kafka component, and says: You asked for Kafka; this scaffold runs on Redis locally so it works without extra infrastructure.
The subscriber Program.cs calls app.UseCloudEvents() before MapPost
